name: TX-25
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with an R+11 partisan lean
Prediction markets give Sims only about a 2% win chance
Williams has a large money edge; Sims shows no reported fundraising
No public general-election polling of the race
model.rationale: An R+11 district, Roger Williams' million-dollar cash advantage, and market pricing that gives Dione Sims roughly a 2% chance all point to a comfortable Republican hold; with no polling suggesting competition, the real question is the size of the margin rather than the winner.
model.watch: A late influx of Democratic spending or a strong statewide Texas trend toward Democrats could narrow the margin, though an outright upset would require an abrupt change in the race's fundamentals.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 25th District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Roger Williams is seeking another term with the advantages that typically come with it. He has raised about $1.4 million and enters the general election with roughly $1.1 million on hand, while Democrat Dione Sims shows no reported fundraising in the available data. No public polls of the race have surfaced, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Sims only about a 2% chance of winning, consistent with a district that favored Republicans by eleven points at the presidential level. The main question is not which party wins but the size of the margin, which will depend heavily on turnout across the exurban Dallas-Fort Worth territory that makes up most of the seat. Barring an unexpected shift, Williams is positioned for a comfortable re-election.
